speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Athletes' Achievement Award (AAA) is managed by the Singapore National Paralympic Council (SNPC) and funded by sponsors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The scheme was initiated by the Singapore Disability Sports Council in 2002 to recognise the achievements of Team Singapore medallists at Major Games, such as the Paralympics, Asian Para Games, Commonwealth Games and the ASEAN Para Games.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Singapore National Olympic Council (SNOC) offers the Multi-Million Dollar Award Programme (MAP) for athletes who have medalled at Major Games, such as the Olympics, Asian Games and South East Asian Games, since 1991.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The AAA and MAP are decided, respectively and separately, by SNPC, SNOC and their sponsors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is in line with the general convention that monetary rewards for competitions in sports are largely funded by private means through sponsorships, donations and product endorsements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As Member Mr Alex Yam has suggested, beyond monetary rewards, there are other meaningful ways in which Singapore society can support and recognise the efforts of our Paralympians.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Some woke up early to tune in to "live" broadcasts to cheer on our own Team Singapore Paralympians in Rio.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: When the athletes returned, Singaporeans turned out in force to welcome them at the airport and to cheer them on during the Celebration Parade.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: On the Government's part, Yip Pin Xiu was inducted into the Sports Hall of Fame in 2015, standing alongside legends like Tan Howe Liang and Fandi Ahmad.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In 2008, she was honoured with one of the nation's highest accolades, the Meritorious Service Medal, in recognition of her first Gold medal at the Beijing Paralympics.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Similarly, Joseph Schooling will be honoured with the Meritorious Service Medal for his first Olympic Gold medal at Rio.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I agree with the Member that our para-athletes demonstrate tremendous resilience and strength of spirit and that we have much to learn from them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Sport Singapore (SportSG) has been profiling their journeys on social media and other platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mediacorp has also broadcasted documentaries on Yip Pin Xiu and Theresa Goh recently in this regard.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will continue to share their inspiring stories with the public.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Next month, I hope Members will join me in Parliament when I move a Motion to congratulate our Paralympians for their excellent performance in Rio and celebrate their achievements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To put the issue in perspective, what can make a difference to our national athletes – whether Olympian or Paralympian – is the combined assistance they receive from family, the community, corporates, the public and the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: When all stakeholders work towards a common objective, we provide a strong and sustainable eco-system of support for them to pursue their sporting aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Both Joseph and Pin Xiu have shown us the importance of family support.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To enable this, SportSG has the SpexBusiness Network.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As part of the scheme, for example, Deloitte provides quality opportunities to our national athletes, both able-bodied and those with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I encourage corporates and well-wishers to complement the roles that the Government plays in building up a sustainable eco-system of support for all our Team Singapore athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: On the Government's part, our main role is to provide opportunities for all Singaporeans to pursue their sporting aspirations and achieve their full potential.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Hence, our focus has been on providing a sustained, structured and comprehensive support system to help our Team Singapore athletes for podium positions at major games.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Instead of focusing on post-podium rewards, we believe our role is to support our athletes upfront in their journey to the podium.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We want more of them to get to the podium and bring pride to the nation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We support them through providing scholarships that pay them reasonably well to train full-time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We fund the National Sports Associations (NSAs) and Singapore Sports Institute so that the athletes can be guided by experienced professional coaches, physiotherapists and sports scientists, as they constantly challenge themselves to do better, swim faster, sail faster.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And we have been expanding the scale of our programme at a sustainable pace over the last few years.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: SportSG would not be able to help as many aspiring athletes pursue their dreams if it had to divert resources to fund post-competition award schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked whether the Government should provide para-athletes with the same level of infrastructural, funding and training support as able-bodied athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: First, we value all our Team Singapore athletes tremendously.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They inspire us as a nation, not just with their sporting achievements, but through their hard work, determination, perseverance, fighting spirit and commitment to excel.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These are values that the nation should embrace and the Government is committed to nurturing our Team Singapore athletes, of all abilities, to reach their full potential.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Second, we do not discriminate between able-bodied athletes and para-athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The "team behind the team" of sports medicine and sports science specialists, psychologists and trainers under SportSG supporting these two groups of athletes is the same.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Sports like equestrian, rowing or shooting may require more funding to support the transport of equipment for overseas competitions, like horses, boats and rifles.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Some para-athletes may need to be accompanied by a caregiver constantly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: When Team Singapore athletes of all abilities go into the sporting arena, flying our flag high, they need our full support.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Government is fully behind our athletes and we encourage corporates and the public to also lend their support, so that we can best cheer them on together as One Team Singapore.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Are you also taking Question Nos 4 and 5 together or just Question No 3?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government has said that it requested the Council to review the awards scheme.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As I have said earlier on, these two awards are handled by two of these NGOs separately.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These two NGOs will have their own agenda and timeline, and I am sure they will take this review quite seriously.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But, more importantly is that they need to have conversations with the donors and supporters because both organisations may have different needs and objectives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think it is best to leave them to look at their overall plan.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SNPC has just had a new President elected.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I am sure he has to find his feet and get on with his work.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I believe there is some amount of confusion among the public in terms of the amount that our Paralympians are receiving.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My second question is on sponsors for the SNPC as well as the SNOC.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I believe that Tote Board and Singapore Pools are major sponsors of both the AAA as well as the MAP.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Is the value that Tote Board is providing to both these awards equivalent and, if it is not so, would they be willing to bring this up to speed?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Minister also mentioned the importance of a whole-of-society approach.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I met Deloitte recently and I think they are doing a wonderful job in helping many of our athletes in terms of their future career.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What plans are there in place at the Ministry level to encourage, in a more concrete manner, more of such corporations to come on board, especially local corporations?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Lastly, the Minister also mentioned the number of carded athletes.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Are any of the current Paralympians also receiving scholarships?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The scheme by SNOC, on the other hand, is different.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As far as sponsors are concerned, yes, Tote Board and Singapore Pools are the two main sponsors at this point in time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But if you look back at the history of these two awards, actually the two organisations have been working with several donors in the past and, for various reasons, the 	Page: 24 donors have been coming in and out of the schemes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But at this juncture, with the very tremendous achievements that our athletes have put in, both at the Rio 2016 Summer Olympics and the Paralympics, we would really like to encourage the corporates to step up again to support our athletes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, it started off as a scheme that had multiple sponsors, all like-minded and wanting to give our athletes an encouragement and a push.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I would urge corporates to step up again.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The athletes whom we speak to are actually looking at internships and employment where companies can allow them to make a living and, at the same time, accommodate their training and competition schedule.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They are also looking at accumulating experience that will serve them well as they retire from their sporting career.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, it is important for companies to also step forward to look at the values that our athletes have displayed ‒ values that are very much treasured by companies these days – teamwork, resilience, confidence.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These are really good values that will serve the companies well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I hope that companies will be encouraged to follow the practice of Deloitte and other companies that have come on board our spexBusiness Network.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The spexBusiness Network is one of the schemes where MCCY, through SportSG, encourages corporates to step forward with internship and employment opportunities, and we recognise them.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Annually, we will have an opportunity to thank them formally.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We also welcome companies which are prepared to offer their services to some of these Institutes of Public Character (IPCs) or National Sports Associations (NSAs).

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many of the NSAs are also in need of professional services that can help them raise their level of management.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And, as you know, in the last Budget, we have improved our incentive schemes for corporations, either through donations or through contributions of their services, to claim deductions for their taxes as well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To answer Mr Alex Yam's specific questions about carding athletes and whether our para-athletes are carded, the answer is yes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I believe we have about 120 para-athletes who are carded at the moment and many of our Paralympians have been on full support from Spex schemes for several years.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Nurul has gone through two cycles, supported by us, and Sze Ning as well for the latest cycle in Rio.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But, of course, I must admit that the full-time Spex Scholarships were put in place from 2013 onwards.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, it is something that we have done since 2013.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Does the Government believe that the Paralympians should be equally rewarded?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I believe I have devoted quite a significant part of my answer to that question.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And the kind of support ‒ in terms of sports science, sports medicine, physiotherapists, psychologists, counsellors ‒ it is all the same.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, our focus is to help as many athletes as possible in their journey onto the podium.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And what is after the podium is for every one of us to put in our share to stand behind them and to cheer them on.
